t:
Subchapter X of chapter 47 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 931 (article 131 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), the following new section (article):“§ 931a. Art. 131a. Subornation of perjury“(a) In General.—Any person subject to this chapter who induces and procures another person—“(1) to take an oath; and“(2) to falsely testify, depose, or state upon such oath;shall, if the conditions specified in subsection (b) are satisfied, be punished as a court-martial may direct.“(b) Conditions.—The conditions referred to in subsection (a) are the following:“(1) The oath is administered with respect to a matter for which such oath is required or authorized by law.“(2) The oath is administered by a person having authority to do so.“(3) Upon the oath, the other person willfully makes or subscribes a statement.“(4) The statement is material.“(5) The statement is false.“(6) When the statement is made or subscribed, the person subject to this chapter and the other person do not believe that the statement is true.”
.

fable.w: This section adds a criminal offense (subornation of perjury) to the Uniform Code of Military Justice and defines its elements and punishment. The tempting reading is that references to testimony, oaths, and court-martial imply a hearing-like process, but these describe elements of a crime and military adjudication, not consultation with outside parties before a federal decision. No comment period, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: shall, if the conditions specified in subsection (b) are satisfied, be punished as a court-martial may direct.

opus.w: This section adds a criminal offense to the Uniform Code of Military Justice and leaves punishment to a court-martial, which is part of the federal government. The references to oaths and testimony describe what counts as the crime. They do not set up any process for people outside the government to consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. No outside party is brought into any decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: Any person subject to this chapter who induces and procures another person—“(1) to take an oath; and“(2) to falsely testify, depose, or state upon such oath;shall, if the conditions specified in subsection (b) are satisfied, be punished as a court-martial may direct.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Words like "oath," "testify," and "court-martial" sound procedural, which might suggest outsiders are taking part in a federal process. That reading fails the definition. The section only creates a military crime, subornation of perjury, for people subject to the Uniform Code of Military Justice. Punishment is decided inside the military justice system. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the criminal offense of subornation of perjury under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. It does not require or recommend consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities in a federal decision-making process. The 'other person' mentioned is a witness in a legal proceeding, not an outside party providing input on a policy or administrative decision. The definition of participation focuses on pre-decision consultation or rights to object/sue, neither of which is present here.
qwen_chat.s: Any person subject to this chapter who induces and procures another person—(1) to take an oath; and (2) to falsely testify, depose, or state upon such oath; shall, if the conditions specified in subsection (b) are satisfied, be punished as a court-martial may direct.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "other person" who testifies is an outside party participating in a legal process. However, the definition of participation requires consultation or coordination *before* a federal decision is made, or the granting of a right to sue/object to a decision. This section defines a criminal offense (subornation of perjury) and sets out the conditions for punishment. It does not establish a process for public input, advisory committees, or consultation with non-federal entities regarding a government decision. The "other person" is a witness in a legal proceeding, not a participant in the administrative or policy-making sense defined here. Furthermore, the actors involved (persons subject to the Uniform Code of Military Justice) are generally federal personnel (military members), and the process is judicial/military justice, not administrative participation.
